raw_response:
I am still doing cotton on all 3 mu this year. I am old now, so I do not want to toss things around too much. Cotton is what I know, and on this little land I would rather keep a steady hand than chase something new. In our place, if I miss the season or save too much on fertilizer, the cotton shows it later and I cannot make it back. Last year the field where I put a bit more base fertilizer held better, so this year I will still put base fertilizer first, then add a little at squaring and flowering. I have well water, but pumping costs money, so I will not irrigate too many times. I will watch the rain and the soil moisture.

My children and younger people have some off-farm work, so for daily management I mainly count on myself and a few family members when work is tight, especially planting and picking. Cotton takes more hand work than wheat or maize, but on 3 mu we can still manage it. I will use improved seed I can buy locally, plant around mid-April, keep the field clean early with herbicide, and then watch insects closely in summer. I do not want to spend too much cash at the start, but I also do not dare cut inputs too hard, because if cotton grows weak the yield drops fast.
